title: Investigative talking points
rankingMethod: Editorial triage by evidence strength, allocation scale and verifiable next question; not corruption likelihood or a statistical risk score. Amounts overlap; do not add them.

findings.title: RCS: identical budget packages across unequal rainfall proxies
findings.basis: Direct allocation observation; rainfall need remains a proxy
findings.question: What policy or engineering design justifies one identical budget unit per office?
findings.evidence: All district-office RCS lines have the same amount. Province/regional rainfall proxies differ by 2.59×. Alternative formulas move different numbers of budget units. All 199 DEO lines are retained unchanged in HGAB; no differentiated needs weighting is visible in the amounts.
findings.alternative: Standard package costs or a minimum coverage policy may justify equal allocations. Rainfall alone does not measure demand.
findings.next: Obtain siting, design capacity, water demand, catchment area and existing RCS inventory.
findings.caution: DEO is not LEG; province rainfall is not a district observation. Returning FY2026 program.

findings.title: Two NEP matching screens give different candidate counts
findings.lead: 5,549 supplied-comparison rows vs 6,105 / 15,979 native project rows
findings.basis: Source and matcher reconciliation; not a confirmed insertion count
findings.question: Which source rows explain the difference between the supplied comparison and the native one-to-one screen?
findings.evidence: The supplied comparison marks 5,549 domestic rows without a plausible NEP title counterpart, carrying ₱158.363B. The native one-to-one screen selects no NEP counterpart for 6,105 of 15,979 HGAB project rows. The 556-row difference is not a count of missing projects: the screens use different matching rules and row populations.
findings.alternative: Different project filters, grouped occurrences, parser boundaries, source versions and matching rules can change candidate counts.
findings.next: Reconcile project IDs and source pages, align project-level denominators, then adjudicate a sample against the original NEP and HGAB pages.
findings.caution: Neither count is a certified insertion total, and the counts are not independent confirmations of the same set of projects.

findings.title: Multi-purpose buildings: a large share needs NEP counterpart review
findings.question: Which MPB lines are genuinely new, and what documented facility needs and designs support them?
findings.evidence: The HGAB MPB PAP contains 5,765 lines carrying ₱83.707B. 620 counterpart cases remain separate from insertion candidates. The historical screen has 329 comparison pairs covering 301 distinct NEP proposals.
findings.alternative: Renaming, combined occurrences and legitimate phased construction can explain unmatched or recurring titles. Similar amounts can reflect standard designs.
findings.next: Audit original NEP/HGAB pages; obtain building purpose, floor area, design, quantities, contract scope and completion records.
findings.caution: MPB overlaps the full DPWH insertion/repeat findings; do not add their amounts. Equal allocations are not equal construction unit prices.

findings.title: Recurring project titles: inspect overlapping work before alleging duplication
findings.lead: 634 of 736 NEP comparison pairs clearly retained in HGAB
findings.question: Are new appropriations paying for already-funded components or legitimate continuation?
findings.evidence: 591 of 685 distinct NEP repeat-screen proposals have clear HGAB links. 22 proposals have explicit overlapping historical chainage. ₱27.255B is the unique NEP proposal allocation, not alleged loss.
findings.alternative: Multi-year implementation, rehabilitation and distinct components can share names and segments.
findings.next: Prioritize explicitly overlapping retained proposals and high amounts; compare contracts, quantities, tranche scopes and completion.
findings.caution: The 737 headline counts NEP–old GAA comparison pairs. Potential retention and missing counterparts remain separate.

findings.title: Exact ₱5M road and flood allocations cluster in the same offices
findings.lead: 35 overlapping offices vs 21.7 expected under independence
findings.question: Does standard design, office workload or coordinated allocation explain the co-occurrence?
findings.evidence: Office odds ratio 5.34; unadjusted exact p=5.07e-06. Region-controlled result is also unusual under its stated null.
findings.alternative: Common specifications, office workload and project mix can create clustering.
findings.next: Pre-specify work-type and workload controls; inspect quantities and comparable prior-year prices.
findings.caution: Threshold/category selection was post hoc. Association does not establish procurement splitting or intent.

findings.title: INSPIRE: a large returning named appropriation needs a whole-project ledger
findings.question: What is the total approved cost and which unfinished components explain the new appropriation?
findings.evidence: Named GAA lines exist in FY2023 and FY2025; FY2027 is not a first appearance.
findings.alternative: A legitimate phased project can require multiple appropriations.
findings.next: Obtain total project cost, phases, progress, obligations, disbursements and procurement records.
findings.caution: Appropriations are not actual spending; stage/year sums do not prove duplication.

findings.title: Length and chainage gaps limit budget scrutiny
findings.lead: Roads: 48.64% · Bridges: 94.39% · FMR: 99.69% without usable extracted length
findings.basis: Extracted metadata coverage; original-document completeness unverified
findings.question: Can the funded segment and engineering length be established for every allocation?
findings.evidence: Roads: 3,329/6,482 lines have derivable stated lengths · Bridges: 65/1,159 lines have derivable stated lengths · FMR: 3/964 lines have derivable stated lengths. Official programs have separate denominators on the supporting page.
findings.alternative: Lengths may be recorded in engineering schedules or continuation text not recovered by this extraction; incomplete metadata need not reflect deliberate omission.
findings.next: Inspect original source pages and obtain funded-segment boundaries, complete chainage, project quantities and bridge spans; reconcile extraction gaps before alleging disclosure failures.
findings.caution: Missing includes absent and unusable extracted evidence, not proof the original documents lack length. Coordinate distances do not establish construction length; mixed scopes are separate.

detailLinks.label: Missing-length coverage by category and program

findings.title: Allocation per stated meter: inspect scope before comparing rates
findings.lead: 189 road and 2 bridge high-rate candidates · FMR peers insufficient
findings.basis: Descriptive allocation/segment-length proxy; comparable engineering costs unavailable
findings.question: Do apparently high rates reflect short printed segments, structures, broader funded scope, or unusually costly comparable work?
findings.evidence: Whole HGAB line-item allocation is divided by its derivable stated segment meters. Roads, bridges and FMR are displayed separately, with official work-program filters. Mixed road/bridge lines receive no single-work rate. Data-derived length groups and within-program slope-change screens are provided; no fixed 100-meter boundary is imposed. Lane evidence now supports 3 title-stated lane rates, 279 stated-length inventory lane estimates, and 390 existing-bridge asset lane estimates. These bases are shown separately and are not pooled into the per-meter flags. Recorded-condition screening identifies 2 rehabilitation lines on fully matched Good/Fair assessed road segments and 0 pavement-work lines within the disclosed five-budget-year surfacing window. These are review leads; later deterioration and different work scope may justify the allocations.
findings.alternative: Terrain, width, structures, approaches, rehabilitation scope and components outside the stated segment can explain large differences. Tiny printed ranges or parser errors can produce extreme ratios.
findings.next: Verify station endpoints on original pages, then compare quantities, width, funded extent, designs and bill-of-quantity costs within the same work type. Investigate unusually short denominators before interpreting extreme ratios.
findings.caution: These are appropriations per stated segment meter, not verified construction unit costs. Bridge chainage is not necessarily bridge span. No cross-category average, overpricing estimate or corruption probability is established. Inventory lanes are existing asset characteristics, not verified funded quantities; widening needs additional funded lanes. Overpasses, flyovers and viaducts use bridge peers.

findings.title: Very short printed road ranges need engineering clarification
findings.lead: 3 checked road ranges imply less than 5 meters
findings.basis: Original PDF text agreement; funded engineering extent unresolved
findings.question: Do the printed station endpoints correctly describe the funded segment, or do notation and scope need correction?
findings.evidence: Original-page visible text agrees with sampled road titles whose station differences calculate to 0.587 meters, 1.49 meters, 4.67 meters. Across all 3,175 known road lengths, only 204 (6.43%) are below 100 meters; high-rate sorting concentrates short denominators at the top.
findings.alternative: A source-document typo, station convention, short component within a larger project, or broader funded scope can explain these values. A very short printed range does not establish the physical length actually funded.
findings.next: Request corrected or certified station endpoints, funded-segment plans, engineering quantities and allocation scope; verify notation before interpreting extreme allocation-per-meter rates.
findings.caution: This is a printed-range/denominator issue, not evidence that most road projects are short or overpriced. Sampled title agreement rules out a title-transcription mismatch for those examples, not source errors or engineering ambiguity. Bridge lengths require separate interpretation.

findings.title: HGAB 3rd projects without a selected NEP counterpart
findings.basis: One-to-one stage matching screen; unmatched rows require source review
findings.question: Which HGAB 3rd projects are genuinely absent from NEP after title, scope and occurrence review?
findings.evidence: The current one-to-one comparison selected no NEP counterpart for these project rows. The comparison uses title and scope signals; unresolved and unmatched cases are not proof of new projects.
findings.alternative: Renaming, title wrapping, scope changes, occurrence aggregation and parser errors can prevent counterpart selection.
findings.next: Review NEP and HGAB source pages side by side, then reconcile project scope, office, location and amount.
findings.caution: No selected counterpart means a review candidate, not a confirmed insertion.

findings.title: HGAB 3rd projects with no listed DPWH Transparency documents
findings.basis: DPWH Transparency FY2027 snapshot; local title reconciliation
findings.question: Are project documents available through another route, or should document links be added to the Transparency record?
findings.evidence: Rows without a matched transparency entry listing one or more documents are counted, including titles that do not match the snapshot.
findings.alternative: Documents may be available on another official page or not yet indexed in the captured snapshot.
findings.next: Verify the project identifier and query the responsible DPWH office for POW, geotagged photos and RDC records.
findings.caution: No listed document is a disclosure gap in this snapshot; it does not establish that no document exists.

findings.title: Incomplete documentation: missing POW, geotagged photos or RDC
findings.basis: Locally inspected attachment metadata; HGAB 3rd title matches
findings.question: Which listed attachment types are absent, and can DPWH provide the missing POW, photos or RDC?
findings.evidence: Counts cover only title-matched HGAB projects whose attachment metadata is locally inspected. The supporting section breaks missing POW, photos and RDC out separately.
findings.alternative: The local snapshot may be incomplete, and an attachment may be indexed under another type or record.
findings.next: Review each project’s transparency entry and request missing categories from the implementing office.
findings.caution: Uninspected projects are unknown, not counted as missing; the missing-type groups can overlap.

highRateScreen.method: Peers share category, structure group (overpasses/flyovers, viaducts and pedestrian structures separated), official PAP, a data-derived length band, and matched surface/condition/assessment-year context. Unknown context is pooled only with unknown context and remains explicitly unadjusted. At least 20 peers with stated length ≥10m. Candidate rate exceeds both 2× peer median and Q3+1.5×IQR. Chart extremes exceed max(2×median,Q3+3×IQR); sub-10m printed ranges also stay off rate charts. Lane inventory estimates do not enter these per-meter flags.
highRateScreen.limits: Exploratory relative-rate screen, not proof of overpricing. Width, terrain, structures, engineering quantities and funded extent remain unverified. Missing or insufficient peers produce no high-rate conclusion.

assetConditionContext.method: Condition flag: rehabilitation/reconstruction/major repair only, full matched road range assessed Good/Fair with a known pre-budget assessment year. Recent-surfacing flag: rehabilitation, preventive maintenance or other explicitly described pavement work where the full matched range has a positive recorded last-surfacing year within five budget years; unknown/zero values are not filled. Widening, approaches, slope/drainage and off-carriageway scopes excluded. Bridge condition is displayed, but an unknown assessment year prevents the dated flag.
assetConditionContext.limits: Review leads, not proof of waste or incorrect prioritization. Assessment and budget dates differ; later deterioration, structural/safety work or different funded components may justify rehabilitation. Last-surfacing inventory is older and cannot establish that no later work occurred.

scope: FY2027 NEP/HGAB 3rd reading; historical GAA comparisons where locally available. No GAB/GAA 2027 outcome inferred.

lineItemReviewQueue.ranking: Flag count descending, allocation pesos descending, occurrence ID ascending for exact ties.
lineItemReviewQueue.scope: Domestic DPWH HGAB 3rd-reading occurrences only; not a ranking of the entire national budget.

method.amountGroupScope: Identical PAP and positive exact peso amount; counts are allocation occurrences, not certified distinct construction contracts.
method.historicalMatch: Identical full normalized title after complete trailing metadata removal; same qualified municipality/province; direction/location/tranche conflict and disjoint stated chainage excluded.
method.weights: One point per flag type. Multiple historical years do not add points.
method.highMeterRate: Peers share category, structure group (overpasses/flyovers, viaducts and pedestrian structures separated), official PAP, a data-derived length band, and matched surface/condition/assessment-year context. Unknown context is pooled only with unknown context and remains explicitly unadjusted. At least 20 peers with stated length ≥10m. Candidate rate exceeds both 2× peer median and Q3+1.5×IQR. Chart extremes exceed max(2×median,Q3+3×IQR); sub-10m printed ranges also stay off rate charts. Lane inventory estimates do not enter these per-meter flags.
method.laneEvidence: Title lane rates, inventory lane estimates and existing-bridge asset estimates are separate contextual measures. None adds a ranking point or replaces a missing funded length. Lane and station evidence is retained in lengthReview.

conditionAndSurfacing.method: Condition flag: rehabilitation/reconstruction/major repair only, full matched road range assessed Good/Fair with a known pre-budget assessment year. Recent-surfacing flag: rehabilitation, preventive maintenance or other explicitly described pavement work where the full matched range has a positive recorded last-surfacing year within five budget years; unknown/zero values are not filled. Widening, approaches, slope/drainage and off-carriageway scopes excluded. Bridge condition is displayed, but an unknown assessment year prevents the dated flag.
conditionAndSurfacing.limits: Review leads, not proof of waste or incorrect prioritization. Assessment and budget dates differ; later deterioration, structural/safety work or different funded components may justify rehabilitation. Last-surfacing inventory is older and cannot establish that no later work occurred.

method.evidenceGaps: Missing length and insufficient peers are cautions, not points. A sub-10m printed range gets a separate denominator-warning point and remains subject to source verification. Extreme rates require denominator/scope review and are omitted from rate charts.
method.summaryCoverage: The queue has up to twelve possible flags: the prior nine screening types plus separate incomplete-documentation flags for missing POW, geotagged photos, and RDC among locally inspected attachment records. Potential NEP counterpart and no listed documents are separate flags; document-type flags are unknown outside inspected metadata.
method.dependence: Historical recurrence and chainage overlap are related indicators; scores are descriptive triage, not independent evidence or probabilities.
limitations: Uniform packages can be legitimate. Exact appropriation amounts are not unit costs.
Strict historical matching misses paraphrased titles and unresolved locations; no icon means this screen did not identify a review trigger, not that the project is verified.
The prior-year search uses locally available DPWH road, bridge, building and flood records, not every agency/year.
Matching/parser errors can produce insertion flags. Top 25 overlap other findings; do not sum them as losses.
Current office, representative, role and party do not contribute any points.

districtComparisonPolicy.scope: All district rows are available for reader selection in the all-district ranking. No selected-district section or person-specific defaults.

localDatasetInventory.use: Potential socio-economic context; no year/definition recorded in the inspected rows, so not used as a needs control.
Historical project reference; not a current flood-exposure or FY2027 needs denominator.
